text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- All formal prerequisites for a linkage of the markka to the ERM will exist this weekend.
- Retailers' organisation would like to end ban on give-aways as a marketing device.
- One in two Finns will get a tax rebate this year, for a total of 6.7 billion markka.
- Heirs of John Wayne miffed at Finnish Centre Party's use of scene from an old Wayne movie in an election campaign ad without permission.
- Strong winds halted high-speed passenger ship traffic between Helsinki and Tallinn on Monday. All departures by catamaran and hydrofoil vessels were cancelled.
- Philips has lured key employees away from competitors in a bid to challenge big three mobile phone makers Nokia , Ericsson and Motorola .
- Finland's Tommi Makinen clinched world rally title after winning the Australian rally at the weekend.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Justice ministry planning a less costly and quicker way to wind up small firms. Current procedure can cost business owner thousands of markka.
- New York Stock Exchange spokesman says 15-20 Finnish firms could be listed on Wall Street by the year 2000.
- Merrill Lynch has upgraded Finnish software company TT Tieto to a buy recommendation.
DEMARI
- Finland's consul in Los Angeles, author Jorn Donner, says EU's meddling in culture likely to create "Europudding".
AAMULEHTI
- Weak job skills forcing many Finnish construction workers out of Germany. Experts say previous boom in the building sector to blame for falling standards.
- Survival rate among Finnish cancer patients is one of the highest in the world, according to Finland's cancer registry.
- Depletion of ozone layer above the North pole and Finland continues at record pace, meteorolgist says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finland's Lutheran Church is firmly opposed to further deregulation of Sunday business hours.
- Finland needs 50,000 new private business owners to solve unemployment problem, said businessman Jalo Paananen.
- Trade between countries of the Baltic Sea region grew by an estimated 20 percent last year.
